title: Salt and Sigil Again
premise: Astrid Brightwater's ledgers record the Salt Guild's impossible trades, including a contract she signed as a child to pay her mother's debts. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, she discovers the guild has been selling souls to the Undercourt beneath the mountain to keep its own wards lit — and hers is the final payment due. To save herself and the coastal city of Greyharbor, Astrid must descend into the court and steal back every soul on the ledger, including the one already sold: her mentor Tam's. She succeeds by rewriting the contracts with a sigil of her own invention, unmaking the guild's power, and chooses a new life among the wardless, starlit poor rather than return to the temple that bound her.
about_author: Dominic Vane is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers in northern port towns. Their fiction blends bureaucratic precision with folkloric dread, exploring what ordinary people owe to institutions that claim to protect them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She balances the Salt Guild's books, cataloguing trades in bottled tides and borrowed years, while quietly copying forbidden pages for herself. Her debt-contract sits in the archive, signed in her childhood hand. Emotional beat: restless competence masking a life too small for her.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The border wards fail at moonrise; the sky goes black star by star, and panic floods Greyharbor. The guild masters seal their doors, and Astrid finds Tam's name newly entered in the soul-ledger — sold that very night. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, his last free night. He confesses he sold his soul willingly to buy the city one more season of wards, and begs Astrid not to follow. She follows anyway, stealing the ledger and a guild seal. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Down the Salt Stair
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Guided by a disgraced ward-smith named Brannoc, she descends the drowned stair beneath the harbor into the Undercourt's antechambers, where traded souls flicker like lanterns. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at the scale of the trade.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She poses as an auditor come to reconcile accounts before the Undercourt's pale magistrates, who cannot lie but twist everything. She locates Tam's soul-vessel and learns her own name is next on the ledger. Emotional beat: terror sharpened by audacity.

chapters.title: Ink That Binds
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. In the mortal world above, he deciphers the guild's founding sigil and realizes it was stolen from the Undercourt long ago — the whole trade is theft repaid with theft. He sends word down through a tide-channel. Emotional beat: guilt becoming purpose.

chapters.title: The Auditor's Gambit
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She offers the magistrates a 'correction': if any contract contains a false term, all are void. They accept, certain the guild's papers are clean. She begins forging discrepancies using her own invented sigil. Emotional beat: gambler's exhilaration over an abyss.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, within the vessel. His soul resists rescue, believing his sacrifice is the only thing holding the wards — until Astrid's message proves the guild lied about the terms. He chooses to testify. Emotional beat: despair yielding to trust.

chapters.title: Void Where Signed
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. Before the full court, she presents the flawed contracts; the magistrates void them all, and the guild's stolen sigil shatters above, plunging Greyharbor's masters into ruin. Tam's soul returns to his body on the stair. Emotional beat: triumph laced with grief for what truth costs.

chapters.title: Starlight, Unowned
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, resolution. The stars return, dimmer but honest; the wards are rebuilt by volunteers, not contracts. Astrid burns her own debt-page and opens a free school of scribes in the harbor district. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not bought.
